summary: Interpreted the two-voter-remainder receipt (check 79d6bcb6f89a41dbbd391a742cdf9916, experiment 5657629e) that the previous turn requested. All five comparisons resolved: the removal left node 1 leading a two-voter configuration (voters=(2 3), singleton false) while node 2 led the same configuration and committed 4 against node 1's 2; because the singleton shortcut could not apply, the removed leader accepted the read into readOnly.unconfirmedReads, broadcast two heartbeats and answered nothing - counting a quorum it is not part of; one heartbeat tick ended its leadership; and the accepted request was then gone with no answer, nothing pending or unconfirmed, and no refusal handed to the caller (the witness comparison violated), while no stale index was handed out. With that, the account now answers both halves of Q2 negatively across four measured configurations: a single remaining voter gets a frozen index immediately (locally, and on the forwarded route as another node's read state), while a larger remainder gets its request accepted and silently lost when the removed leader's leadership ends, so the caller is neither answered with a current index nor refused. The investigation's discriminator now narrows to non-removal routes to the same state (demotion to learner under the same default, a joint transition leaving one voter) and to whether the Node wrapper hands an application the same stale index or the same lost request. Validation reports valid with the investigation discriminator and interpretation effects; no execution was requested this turn, since the remaining quorum-option variant cannot be built in the same fixture - with CheckQuorum the remaining voters' lease keeps them from electing a new leader while the removed leader keeps hearing from them.
